questions.q: What specific gap do OneLake data access roles close that workspace roles can't?
options: Granting access to only specific folders or tables inside one Lakehouse, instead of the whole item
Letting a Viewer become a Workspace Admin
Encrypting data in transit between Fabric and the client
Replacing the need for Microsoft Entra ID authentication
questions.explain: Workspace roles like Contributor or Viewer apply to an entire item or workspace; data access roles scope read (or read/write) access down to specific checked tables and folders within one Lakehouse.

questions.q: Which workspace roles are unaffected by a data access role, because they already have full read/write access to all data in the item?
options: Admin, Member, and Contributor
Viewer only
Everyone, including Viewers
No workspace role is ever affected by a data access role
questions.explain: Admins, Members, and Contributors already have read and write access to all data in a workspace, so data access roles don't change what they can see. Data access roles matter for Viewers and users with limited item-level Read access.

questions.q: In the New role wizard's Data step, what does choosing "Selected data" and then Edit let you do?
options: Check off the exact tables and folders in the Tables/Files directories that the role should grant access to
Delete tables from the Lakehouse permanently
Automatically grant access to every future table added to the Lakehouse
Change the Lakehouse's workspace assignment
questions.explain: "Selected data" plus Edit opens a checklist of the Lakehouse's Tables and Files directories, letting you pick exactly which items the role covers — "All data" is the option that includes future items automatically.

questions.q: What is a "virtual membership" in a OneLake data access role, created through Advanced Configuration?
options: Membership assigned dynamically based on Fabric item permissions a user already holds, rather than a manually maintained list of names
A temporary membership that expires after 24 hours
A membership visible only to Fabric administrators
A role that grants access to virtual machines in Azure
questions.explain: Advanced Configuration lets you add members based on permissions like Read, Write, Reshare, Execute, or ReadAll that they already hold on the item — the membership updates automatically as those permissions change.

questions.q: Why can the built-in DefaultReader role undermine a carefully scoped data access role?
options: DefaultReader gives anyone with ReadAll permission access to all data in the Lakehouse, overriding the narrower role unless it's removed or edited
DefaultReader automatically deletes any role scoped to fewer than three tables
DefaultReader only applies to workspace Admins, so it never affects regular users
DefaultReader disables row-level security on every table
questions.explain: Every Lakehouse ships with a DefaultReader role granting full data access to anyone with ReadAll permission on the item. A user still covered by DefaultReader keeps that broad access even after being added to a narrower role, unless DefaultReader is edited or they're removed from it.
